title: The free tools — the connection to lawful free access
body: Outstanding free tools, legally solid, for books, textbooks, research and media. We are the CONNECTION to them — we host nothing and take nothing; we get you the most, free, through every lawful channel. Everything up to the line, nothing on it.
subject: the free tools

connections.evidence: lawful free access, a spine of the Floor of Discovery

author: Matt Harris (the connection to free tools)

title: Libby / OverDrive — free library
body: Libby / OverDrive: Borrow ebooks and audiobooks FREE from your public library, on your phone. The single best free reading app.  How it's free & legal: public-library lending (licensed).  Go: https://libbyapp.com
subject: Libby / OverDrive
author: Matt Harris (the connection to free tools)

title: Hoopla — free library
body: Hoopla: Ebooks, audiobooks, movies, music, and comics — free, instantly, with a library card; usually no waitlist.  How it's free & legal: public-library lending (licensed).  Go: https://www.hoopladigital.com
subject: Hoopla
author: Matt Harris (the connection to free tools)

title: Kanopy — free library
body: Kanopy: Films and documentaries — Criterion, PBS, indie — streamed free through your library or university.  How it's free & legal: public-library lending (licensed).  Go: https://www.kanopy.com
subject: Kanopy
author: Matt Harris (the connection to free tools)

title: Get a library card online — free library
body: Get a library card online: Many US public libraries issue a card online in minutes; some (e.g. large city systems) enroll non-residents. The master key to everything above.  How it's free & legal: public institution.  Go: https://www.overdrive.com/libraries
subject: Get a library card online
author: Matt Harris (the connection to free tools)

title: OpenStax — free textbooks
body: OpenStax: Free, peer-reviewed college textbooks — biology, physics, calculus, economics, history — openly licensed, keep them forever.  How it's free & legal: CC-BY open license (Rice University).  Go: https://openstax.org
subject: OpenStax
author: Matt Harris (the connection to free tools)

title: MIT OpenCourseWare — free textbooks
body: MIT OpenCourseWare: The actual materials of thousands of MIT courses — lectures, notes, problem sets, exams — free and open.  How it's free & legal: open courseware (CC).  Go: https://ocw.mit.edu
subject: MIT OpenCourseWare
author: Matt Harris (the connection to free tools)

title: LibreTexts — free textbooks
body: LibreTexts: A vast free library of open textbooks across the sciences, humanities and more — remixable and legal.  How it's free & legal: open education (CC).  Go: https://libretexts.org
subject: LibreTexts
author: Matt Harris (the connection to free tools)

title: Open Textbook Library — free textbooks
body: Open Textbook Library: Peer-reviewed open textbooks you can read, download and print free.  How it's free & legal: open license (U. Minnesota).  Go: https://open.umn.edu/opentextbooks
subject: Open Textbook Library
author: Matt Harris (the connection to free tools)

title: OER Commons — free textbooks
body: OER Commons: A search engine for openly-licensed teaching and learning materials at every level.  How it's free & legal: open educational resources (CC).  Go: https://oercommons.org
subject: OER Commons
author: Matt Harris (the connection to free tools)

title: Khan Academy — free textbooks
body: Khan Academy: Free lessons and practice from arithmetic to calculus, grammar to history — for any learner, any age.  How it's free & legal: free nonprofit.  Go: https://www.khanacademy.org
subject: Khan Academy
author: Matt Harris (the connection to free tools)

title: Saylor Academy — free textbooks
body: Saylor Academy: Free, self-paced college-level courses, with free certificates and credit pathways.  How it's free & legal: free nonprofit (CC).  Go: https://www.saylor.org
subject: Saylor Academy
author: Matt Harris (the connection to free tools)

title: Unpaywall — free research
body: Unpaywall: A free browser button that finds the LEGAL open-access version of a paywalled paper — the author's or publisher's own free copy.  How it's free & legal: open access (legal author/publisher copies).  Go: https://unpaywall.org
subject: Unpaywall
author: Matt Harris (the connection to free tools)

title: arXiv — free research
body: arXiv: Free preprints in physics, mathematics, computer science, biology and more — posted by the authors themselves.  How it's free & legal: author-posted preprints (open).  Go: https://arxiv.org
subject: arXiv
author: Matt Harris (the connection to free tools)

title: PubMed Central — free research
body: PubMed Central: Millions of free full-text biomedical and life-sciences articles from the US National Institutes of Health.  How it's free & legal: open access (NIH, public).  Go: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc
subject: PubMed Central
author: Matt Harris (the connection to free tools)

title: DOAJ — free research
body: DOAJ: The Directory of Open Access Journals — vetted, free, peer-reviewed scholarship across every field.  How it's free & legal: open-access journals (peer-reviewed).  Go: https://doaj.org
subject: DOAJ
author: Matt Harris (the connection to free tools)

title: CORE — free research
body: CORE: The world's largest collection of open-access research papers, searchable and free to read.  How it's free & legal: open-access aggregator.  Go: https://core.ac.uk
subject: CORE
author: Matt Harris (the connection to free tools)

title: Google Scholar — free research
body: Google Scholar: Search scholarly literature; the 'All versions' link often surfaces a free, legal PDF.  How it's free & legal: index (links to legal free copies).  Go: https://scholar.google.com
subject: Google Scholar
author: Matt Harris (the connection to free tools)

title: OpenAlex — free research
body: OpenAlex: A free, open index of the world's scholarship — papers, authors, institutions — with links to open copies.  How it's free & legal: open catalog (CC0).  Go: https://openalex.org
subject: OpenAlex
author: Matt Harris (the connection to free tools)

title: WorldCat — free find
body: WorldCat: Find which library near you holds any book, then borrow it free. The map to every library's shelves.  How it's free & legal: library catalog.  Go: https://search.worldcat.org
subject: WorldCat
author: Matt Harris (the connection to free tools)

title: Interlibrary Loan (ILL) — free find
body: Interlibrary Loan (ILL): Ask your library to borrow a book or article from another library for you — usually free. Almost anything can be gotten this way.  How it's free & legal: library cooperation.  Go: https://www.worldcat.org
subject: Interlibrary Loan (ILL)
author: Matt Harris (the connection to free tools)

title: Internet Archive — free find
body: Internet Archive: Millions of PUBLIC-DOMAIN books, films, audio and software, free to download; plus a scan-and-borrow library. A vast lawful commons.  How it's free & legal: public domain + fair use archive.  Go: https://archive.org
subject: Internet Archive
author: Matt Harris (the connection to free tools)

title: HathiTrust — free find
body: HathiTrust: Full text of public-domain works, and full-text SEARCH across millions more — a use the courts ruled lawful fair use.  How it's free & legal: fair use — WON in court (Authors Guild v. HathiTrust).  Go: https://www.hathitrust.org
subject: HathiTrust
author: Matt Harris (the connection to free tools)

extra.legal_basis: fair use — WON in court (Authors Guild v. HathiTrust)

title: Project Gutenberg — free public domain
body: Project Gutenberg: ~77,000 public-domain books, full text, free — the classics of the world, no strings.  How it's free & legal: public domain.  Go: https://www.gutenberg.org
subject: Project Gutenberg
author: Matt Harris (the connection to free tools)

title: Standard Ebooks — free public domain
body: Standard Ebooks: The great public-domain books, lovingly re-typeset into beautiful, free, modern ebook files.  How it's free & legal: public domain (CC0 formatting).  Go: https://standardebooks.org
subject: Standard Ebooks
author: Matt Harris (the connection to free tools)

title: Wikisource — free public domain
body: Wikisource: A free library of source texts — documents, public-domain books, translations — transcribed and proofread.  How it's free & legal: public domain / CC-BY-SA.  Go: https://wikisource.org
subject: Wikisource
author: Matt Harris (the connection to free tools)

title: Library of Congress — Digital — free public domain
body: Library of Congress — Digital: Free digitized books, maps, photographs, recordings and manuscripts from the world's largest library.  How it's free & legal: US government / public domain.  Go: https://www.loc.gov/collections
subject: Library of Congress — Digital
author: Matt Harris (the connection to free tools)

title: Google Books — free public domain
body: Google Books: Read public-domain books in full, and preview and search inside most others — free and lawful.  How it's free & legal: public-domain full view + fair-use preview.  Go: https://books.google.com
subject: Google Books
author: Matt Harris (the connection to free tools)

title: Borrow from your people — free borrow
body: Borrow from your people: The oldest free tool: ask a friend, your church, or a neighbor to lend you their copy — lending a book or disc you own is entirely lawful. Among believers, say what you need and someone near you may already have it on their shelf.  How it's free & legal: personal lending (first-sale doctrine).  Go:
subject: Borrow from your people
author: Matt Harris (the connection to free tools)

title: Musopen — free media
body: Musopen: Free public-domain sheet music and recordings of classical music — legal to use for anything.  How it's free & legal: public domain / CC music.  Go: https://musopen.org
subject: Musopen
author: Matt Harris (the connection to free tools)

title: Free Music Archive — free media
body: Free Music Archive: Free, legal music under Creative Commons licenses — for listening and for making.  How it's free & legal: Creative Commons music.  Go: https://freemusicarchive.org
subject: Free Music Archive
author: Matt Harris (the connection to free tools)

title: The line — lawful free access only
body: THE LINE — what we will and will not connect you to. We point ONLY to lawful free access: public-library lending, open licenses (Creative Commons / OER), the public domain, and fair use that has been upheld in court (as HathiTrust's was). We use everything UP TO that line and nothing on it. We do NOT point to Sci-Hub, Library Genesis, or any piracy — they lost in court, and we keep our hands clean (Romans 13:1; Matthew 22:21). The gift is real precisely because it is legal.
subject: the line
author: Matt Harris (the connection to free tools)
